filename: Deep Learning Based Cloud Cover Parameterization for ICON.pdf
title: Deep Learning Based Cloud Cover Parameterization for ICON
venue: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
parameterization_target: sub-grid scale cloud cover (cloud volume fraction and cloud area fraction)
code_availability: The neural network and analysis code can be found at https://github.com/agrundner24/iconml_clc and is preserved at DOI:10.5281/zenodo.5788873. The software code for the ICON model is available from https://code.mpimet.mpg.de/projects/iconpublic.
testbed_rationale: High-resolution storm-resolving ICON simulations coarse-grained to standard climate model resolutions (R2B4 and R2B5) specifically designed for training and benchmarking ML-based subgrid cloud cover parameterizations, with code publicly archived and sample training data provided on GitHub.
pain_points: Generalization across climate regimes/regions fails when NNs encounter out-of-distribution thermodynamic regimes (e.g. tropical NARVAL trained model extrapolating to cold polar regions).
Non-locality / column models overfit or struggle to transfer across grids compared to neighborhood/local models.
Temporal mismatch in model output variables (~7% cloudy grid cells were condensate-free due to sequential physics calls).
Mixing length error in QUBICC simulation diffusion scheme (set to 1000m instead of 150m) led to unrealistically strong vertical diffusion.
Very large dataset size (several TBs) necessitates aggressive subsampling and memory considerations, which hindered random forests.
extraction_notes: The paper mentions preliminary coupled simulations for one month in the discussion, but the work presented in this study is strictly offline evaluation.
